sentences.text: Sisteronia is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur found in the Middle Cretaceous of southeastern England and France.
This animal possesses three unique traits that distinguish it from all other known platypterygiine ophthalmosaurids.
Its delicate, slender, and unworn teeth suggest it hunted soft-bodied small prey like small fish and neocoleoid cephalopods.
The genus was named by Fischer, Bardet, Guiomar, and Godefroit in 2014 to honor the commune of Sisteron in southeastern France, where relatively complete specimens were collected.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is catalogue number CAMSM B58257_67, designated by the authors in 2014.

Sisteronia belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae and the infraorder Thunnosauria. Fischer et al. assigned it to the subfamily Platypterygiinae because it shares traits with that group and lacks traits of ophthalmosaurine ophthalmosaurids.
This creature lived from the Albian to the Cenomanian stages, between 113.2 and 93.9 million years ago.
